content.text:
**T-5008 has been escalated.** Here's a summary of what I found and why:

---

### Root Cause
`ledger-queue-0` is stuck in `Pending` because its PersistentVolumeClaim (`data-ledger-queue-0`) is bound to a **`local` PersistentVolume** (`local-pv-ip-10-0-7-21-nvme1`). Local volumes require an explicit `nodeAffinity`, and this PV is pinned exclusively to `kubernetes.io/hostname: ip-10-0-7-21.ec2.internal` — the failed node [cite: concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#node-affinity-0]. The scheduler confirms this: *"8 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict"* — every healthy node in the cluster violates this constraint. Because `Pods that use a PV will only be scheduled to nodes that are selected by the node affinity` [cite: concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#node-affinity-0], the pod **cannot schedule anywhere else**, ever, unless the PV's node affinity changes.

### Why This Was Escalated (Data Loss Risk)
There are only two paths forward, and both carry serious risk:

| Path | Data Safety | SLA Risk |
|---|---|---|
| **Wait for node `ip-10-0-7-21` recovery** | ✅ AOF data intact | ⚠️ May miss 15:00 deadline |
| **Delete PVC/PV + re-provision on a healthy node** | ❌ AOF data (buffered settlement messages) permanently destroyed | ✅ Can be done quickly |

The volume's `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Delete` means deleting the PVC also deletes the PV record. The actual AOF data lives on the physical NVMe disk of the dead node — that data contains **unacknowledged settlement messages**, making this a potential financial/compliance data-loss event. This decision requires a business owner and cluster-admin access to create a new local PV on a healthy node, which is beyond the scope of automated resolution.
